_about: Every user-facing Jervis capability, checked against the app's source (ArielZaha/jervis-app). status: download = in the current installer (v1.0.5); next = in the source code, not yet in an installer; source = only when running Jervis from the source code. os: both | mac | win. tools/build_features.py renders this into index.html.

features.name: Wake him by voice
features.summary: Say “Hey Jervis” (or “Wake up Jervis”, “Hello Jervis”). His window opens full screen and he listens.
features.benefit: Hands-free from across the room.

features.name: Speech recognition on your computer
features.summary: Your speech becomes text with Whisper, running locally. Only in the first minutes after installing, while it downloads, is Google’s free recognizer used.
features.benefit: Fast, private, and works offline after the first start.

features.name: Answers out loud, Hebrew too
features.summary: Replies are spoken with your system’s built-in voices and written in the conversation.
features.benefit: Listen while you do something else.
features.needs: On Windows, add the Hebrew voice in Settings, Time & language, Speech to hear Hebrew.

features.name: Type instead of talking
features.summary: The box under the core works exactly like speaking, even with the microphone muted. Press / to jump there; ↑ and ↓ bring back what you typed.
features.benefit: Use him in a quiet room or a noisy one.

features.name: Sleep, mute and interrupt
features.summary: “Goodbye” or “good night” sends him to sleep until you wake him. M mutes the microphone; Space stops him mid-sentence.
features.benefit: He listens only when you want him to.

features.name: Questions, ideas and follow-ups
features.summary: Anything that isn’t a command goes to his AI: explanations, ideas, summaries, translations, advice. He remembers the conversation, so follow-ups work.
features.benefit: One assistant for doing and for asking.

features.name: Several things in one sentence
features.summary: He splits a request into parts, does each in order and answers them together.
features.benefit: Say it the way you think it.

features.name: Forgiving of typos
features.summary: Common misspellings are fixed before he reads a command. The next release recognises many more (“distence”, “greph”, “tell my about saturn”).
features.benefit: Type fast; he still understands.

features.name: His speaking volume
features.summary: Set how loudly he speaks, or mute his voice and read the replies instead (Settings, Voice).
features.benefit: Quiet answers late at night.

features.name: Spotify, the exact song
features.summary: He plays the song, artist or your own playlist in the Spotify app. Free or Premium, no developer keys.
features.benefit: Music by name, without touching the mouse.
features.say: Play my Workout playlist on Spotify
features.needs: The Spotify app, signed in. On a Mac, the Accessibility permission lets him press play for you.

features.name: Albums, liked songs and your mixes
features.summary: “Shuffle my liked songs”, “play the album OK Computer”, Spotify’s mixes by their everyday names (“the repeat playlist”, “discover weekly”, “daily mix 3”), or “a lofi playlist”. Your own playlist always beats a stranger’s with the same name.
features.benefit: Your library, by voice.

features.name: Other music services
features.summary: Apple Music, YouTube Music, SoundCloud, Deezer, Tidal and Amazon Music, by naming the service.
features.benefit: Use the service you already pay for.
features.say: Play OK Computer on Apple Music

features.name: More by the same artist
features.summary: Ask for another song by them and he finds one.
features.benefit: Keep the mood going.

features.name: Pause, skip and go back
features.summary: Pause, resume, next, previous and skip for music and videos.
features.benefit: Control what’s playing from anywhere in the room.
features.needs: On Windows, pause and resume toggle with the media key.

features.name: Jump to a minute
features.summary: “Go to minute 3”, “skip to 2:30”, or start from the beginning.
features.benefit: Find the part you wanted.
features.needs: Mac: in Chrome. Windows: a YouTube or Netflix tab that is the active tab of its window.

features.name: Computer volume
features.summary: Volume up, down, an exact level, or mute.
features.benefit: Too loud? Just say so.

features.name: YouTube
features.summary: Plays a video, a song or a topic on YouTube, reusing one tab.
features.benefit: From a sentence to a playing video.
features.say: Play a video about black holes

features.name: Netflix, down to the episode
features.summary: Starts a show, or an exact season and episode.
features.benefit: No more scrolling through seasons.
features.say: Play Breaking Bad season 3 episode 2 on Netflix

features.name: Stremio
features.summary: Opens a show or movie in Stremio, episodes included.
features.benefit: Your Stremio library by voice.

features.name: Trailers
features.summary: Plays a trailer on YouTube, or Netflix’s own one when you say “on Netflix”.
features.benefit: Decide what to watch faster.
features.say: Show me the trailer of Wednesday

features.name: What should I watch?
features.summary: Ask for suggestions, then refer to them: “show me the trailer of the second one”.
features.benefit: From “I’m bored” to watching.
features.say: Show me the trailer of the second one

features.name: Open any app
features.summary: Any installed app by name, even said imperfectly. On Windows, everything in the Start menu.
features.benefit: Skip the search box.

features.name: Open, then he asks
features.summary: “Open Netflix” asks what to watch; “open Spotify” asks what to listen to; “open Google” asks what to search. Answer and he does it.
features.benefit: A natural back-and-forth, not a command line.

features.name: Websites and search
features.summary: Opens sites like Gmail or Drive, and searches Google.
features.benefit: The web, one sentence away.

features.name: Close apps and tabs by name
features.summary: Close an app, a tab by any word in its title, or all of one site’s tabs. “Close all tabs” asks first.
features.benefit: Tidy up without hunting.
features.needs: Mac: any Chrome tab. Windows: the active tab of a window, in Chrome, Edge, Brave or Firefox.

features.name: School and personal accounts
features.summary: With a Chrome profile for each Google account, school things open in the school one and the rest in the personal one. “Wrong account” moves it.
features.benefit: No more homework in the wrong account.
features.needs: Google Chrome with one profile per account.

features.name: Equations, solved with the steps
features.summary: Linear and quadratic equations are solved by his own code, exactly, as a worksheet: the problem, numbered steps and the answer in a box, typeset like a textbook.
features.benefit: Answers you can trust and learn from.
features.say: Solve x squared minus 5x plus 6 equals 0

features.name: Graph any function
features.summary: Draws the curve with its roots, highs and lows, intercepts and asymptotes marked. Point at it to read any value; Save image keeps a PNG.
features.benefit: See what the function does.
features.say: Graph sine of x over x

features.name: Math follow-ups
features.summary: “Show the steps”, “what’s the vertex?”, “draw the function”, or both at once: “solve 2x + 6 = 0 and draw the graph”.
features.benefit: Keep asking like you would a tutor.

features.name: Two functions on one graph
features.summary: Both curves in their own colours, the points where they meet, the area between them shaded, and how they relate: parallel, perpendicular, tangent, mirrored.
features.benefit: Compare functions at a glance.
features.say: Compare sine of x and cosine of x

features.name: Distances on a 3D globe
features.summary: He finds both places, works out the straight-line distance and draws the route on a turning 3D Earth with clouds and a day–night line. Drag and zoom it.
features.benefit: Geography you can see.
features.say: How far is New York from Tel Aviv?

features.name: Fly the route
features.summary: The camera follows a small plane from departure to destination, with Pause, Replay and Skip. Flight times are labelled estimates.
features.benefit: A trip you can watch.
features.say: How long is the flight from Tel Aviv to New York?

features.name: Countries on the way, and comparisons
features.summary: Which countries a route crosses, from real border data, and which of two places is farther, both routes drawn.
features.benefit: Answers a map can’t give you.
features.say: Which is farther from Tel Aviv, London or New York?

features.name: Nearby places
features.summary: Cities within a distance of a place, from a list of about 7,300 places.
features.benefit: Plan a trip around a city.
features.needs: Small towns may be missing.

features.name: Day, night and sunrise
features.summary: Earth lit by the Sun where it is right now, city lights on the night side, and sunrise and sunset worked out astronomically.
features.benefit: Know whether it’s night where your friend is.

features.name: Planets in 3D
features.summary: Key facts and a lit, spinning model of all eight planets, the Sun, the Moon and Pluto, with real rings on Saturn.
features.benefit: Homework that looks like a planetarium.

features.name: Every graph, globe and planet stays
features.summary: Each one is a small picture in the conversation. ‹ › or the arrow keys step between them; G, E and P show the last graph, globe or planet.
features.benefit: Go back to anything he showed you.

features.name: Weather
features.summary: Ask for the weather anywhere; the current weather also sits in a card in his window. No account or key.
features.benefit: Know before you go out.

features.name: Full forecast window
features.summary: Now (feels-like, humidity, wind, UV), a map with rain radar, the next 24 hours and 7 days.
features.benefit: The whole picture in one view.

features.name: Timers and reminders
features.summary: Set, check and cancel timers and reminders. When one ends his window comes to the front, even if he was asleep, and timers survive a restart.
features.benefit: Never burn the eggs again.
features.say: Remind me in an hour to call Mom

features.name: Google Calendar
features.summary: Hear your next five events, or create one: he asks for the title, date, time and length.
features.benefit: Your schedule without opening it.
features.needs: A one-time free Google sign-in setup in Settings.

features.name: Events in one sentence, with reminders
features.summary: He works out the title, date, time and length himself, asks only for what’s missing, and offers a reminder.
features.benefit: One sentence, one event.
features.say: Add a dentist appointment tomorrow at 5pm

features.name: Apple Calendar
features.summary: Events can go to the Calendar app on a Mac instead of Google Calendar.
features.benefit: Use the calendar you already have.

features.name: Documents, written for you
features.summary: He writes it and puts it in a new document. Mac: Word, Pages, TextEdit, Notes or Google Docs. Windows: Word, Notepad or Google Docs.
features.benefit: From idea to document in one sentence.
features.say: Write a poem about the sea in Word
features.needs: Microsoft Word for Word documents.

features.name: Edit it by voice
features.summary: “Make it shorter”, “read it to me”. Or open a blank document first and he asks what to write.
features.benefit: Revise without retyping.

features.name: Ask about a picture
features.summary: Attach, drop or paste an image: describe it, read its text, explain an error, compare two.
features.benefit: A second pair of eyes for screenshots.
features.needs: A free Groq key, or 16 GB of memory for his local vision model.

features.name: Make a picture
features.summary: Describe it and he creates it, free through Pollinations.ai with no key. An OpenAI key gives better results.
features.benefit: Pictures for school, stories or fun.
features.needs: The free service adds a small watermark and limits how often you can use it.

features.name: Edit a picture
features.summary: “Remove the person in the background”, “make this black and white”. The original is never overwritten.
features.benefit: Quick fixes without an editor.
features.needs: An OpenAI key with billing credit.

features.name: Better picture prompts
features.summary: He expands a short request into a detailed description first, and can use a free Cloudflare account for sharper images.
features.benefit: Better pictures from fewer words.

features.name: Unlimited pictures on your computer
features.summary: A local image model, with no service and no limit.
features.benefit: Pictures that never leave your computer.
features.needs: Running from source with the local-images option; several GB, about 16 GB of memory.

features.name: He uses the mouse and keyboard
features.summary: Ask for something on screen and he works like a person: reads the window, does one thing, checks what changed, continues.
features.benefit: Hand off the boring clicks.
features.say: Use my computer to turn on dark mode in Chrome
features.needs: Mac: the Accessibility permission. The local AI handles short tasks; a free Groq key handles longer ones.

features.name: Always visible, instantly stoppable
features.summary: A glowing edge and a bar with Pause and Stop stay on screen. Move the mouse, press Ctrl+Alt+Q, or say “stop”. He asks before sending, buying, deleting or installing, and never types into password fields.
features.benefit: You stay in charge the whole time.

features.name: Ask first, allowed, or off
features.summary: Choose whether he asks before every task (the default), just does it, or never touches the mouse.
features.benefit: As much control as you’re comfortable with.

features.name: Sees the screen privately
features.summary: He reads windows through your system’s accessibility features. Screenshots are only looked at by his local vision model unless you turn the online option on.
features.benefit: Screen help without uploading your screen.
features.needs: Local vision needs 16 GB of memory.

features.name: Visible Spotify control
features.summary: “Take control and play X on Spotify” is done on screen, step by step, so you can watch.
features.benefit: See exactly what he does.

features.name: Blender, by voice
features.summary: Everyday 3D commands run directly: create a cube, make it twice as big, colour it red, rotate it 45 degrees, delete it, undo.
features.benefit: Model without hunting through menus.
features.say: Create a cube and color it red
features.needs: Blender installed.

features.name: Google Classroom
features.summary: Opens Classroom in your school account and tells you which assignments are missing and which are still due.
features.benefit: Know what’s left before the deadline.
features.needs: Reading works on macOS (Chrome, Allow JavaScript from Apple Events); on Windows he opens the page.

features.name: WhatsApp, read-only
features.summary: Reads unread messages aloud, or what one person wrote. He can’t send, reply or mark as read, and messages never go to an AI or the logs.
features.benefit: Catch up without picking up your phone.
features.needs: WhatsApp Desktop and Full Disk Access. Can be turned off in Settings.

features.name: Jervis on your phone
features.summary: A chat app for iPhone and Android, added to your Home Screen, with the same orb. Hold the mic button and talk, or type.
features.benefit: Your assistant in your pocket.

features.name: Pair with one scan
features.summary: Say “connect my phone” and scan the code on your computer. After that a notification with Confirm connects it, from anywhere.
features.benefit: No codes to type.

features.name: Run your computer from your phone
features.summary: “On my computer” sends everything to the Jervis at home: music, apps, documents, computer control. Graphs, planets and the globe open on the phone too.
features.benefit: Start the music from the couch.

features.name: Works with the computer off
features.summary: “On this phone” runs his own brain inside the app: math and graphs, the globe and planets, weather, timers, music and video apps, writing, pictures, calls, maps.
features.benefit: Useful even away from your desk.
features.needs: A free Groq key pasted into the app. A phone can’t let him change its volume or press play inside other apps.

features.name: End-to-end encrypted
features.summary: Phone and computer share a key only they have; the relay in between only passes bytes it can’t read. List or forget paired phones by voice.
features.benefit: Remote control without handing anyone the keys.

features.name: Text-message pairing
features.summary: Optionally, Jervis texts you the first pairing question instead.
features.benefit: Pair without opening a page first.
features.needs: A free Twilio account.

features.name: The voice core
features.summary: A 3D core that changes colour with what he’s doing (ready, listening, thinking, speaking) and pulses with how loudly you speak. It only measures loudness; nothing is recorded.
features.benefit: You always know what he’s doing.

features.name: Conversation and panels
features.summary: The whole conversation on the right; your computer’s processor, memory and battery, the weather and running timers on the left; and ‘Try saying’ ideas you can click.
features.benefit: Everything at a glance.

features.name: Keyboard shortcuts
features.summary: / to type, M to mute, Space to stop him, F for full screen, Esc to close a window, arrows to step between graphs.
features.benefit: Fast for people who like keys.

features.name: Stays ready in the background
features.summary: Closing the window keeps him in the notification area or menu bar, and he can start when you sign in.
features.benefit: Always one phrase away.

features.name: A night sky behind everything
features.summary: His window gets a starfield with shooting stars crossing the whole sky.
features.benefit: A window you’ll like leaving open.

features.name: Jervis Wake
features.summary: A tiny background listener that opens Jervis when it hears the wake phrase, even when he is closed.
features.benefit: Wake him even after quitting.
features.needs: Installed separately with the script in the source code.

features.name: AI on your own computer
features.summary: Answers come from llama3.2 running locally through Ollama, set up for you on the first start. No account, no key, offline afterwards. If you already use Ollama, he uses yours.
features.benefit: Free and private by default.

features.name: Faster with a free key
features.summary: Paste a free Groq key and he answers with a larger online model, falling back to the local AI by himself.
features.benefit: Speed when you want it.

features.name: Choose the local model
features.summary: Use a bigger local model, such as qwen2.5:7b on a 16 GB computer, for better answers.
features.benefit: Trade speed for quality.

features.name: Your data stays local
features.summary: Settings, transcripts and pictures live in his data folder. Conversation logs can be turned off, and the technical logs never contain what you said.
features.benefit: Nothing to sign up for, nothing to leak.

features.name: Sets himself up
features.summary: The first start downloads his AI and speech models with the progress on screen, picks up where it stopped, and has a Try again button. Music, timers and apps work meanwhile.
features.benefit: No terminal, no Python, no fuss.

features.name: Settings for everything
features.summary: Microphone and voice, the wake phrase, which AI answers, computer control, the weather city, privacy, optional services, and starting at sign-in.
features.benefit: Make him yours.
